title: Unpaid wages, the union, and Weatherford's band closing
summary: Jackson says musicians were cheated, praises union president Harry Gray, mentions his years on the local board, and describes the Weatherford job ending when the place was padlocked.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: They did cheat the musicians. Yes, yes, yes.
I lost, I have money spread all over the country.
They had a union then but it wasn't able to.

Yeah, well the union wasn't as strong as it is now and the president wasn't the president we have now. I think Harry Gray is one of the greatest presidents we've had. I may be a little prejudiced because I served as a board of director of Local 20 years, and three years on the trial board. This was 23 consecutive years. Are you still official? No, I was defeated. I was defeated there in December. So getting back to this band, Weatherford, it lasted a little while, about four to six weeks, closed up on a Sunday night. Monday night was paid even, came Monday the place was padlocked. I understand this Dr. Johnson padlocked the place on account of rent. I cannot prove that but I heard that. So later on Joe, I advanced so, Joe figured I advanced and was ready for the big time. Snags, by that time Snags was playing drums and George Field on trombone and he had Busta Bailey and on the, Bonnie Bigard and, let's see, Albert Nicholson. Albert Nicholson and Bonnie Bigard. And the bass player was Jackson, the fellow played the bass tuba. He didn't have the string bass.
